condition: lateral epicondylitis outer elbow tendon pain gripping tools for 4 weeks
level_rationale: Four weeks of sharp pain on the outer side of the right elbow provoked whenever a 44-year-old carpenter grips hand tools during daily work indicates subacute occupational lateral elbow extensor tendinopathy warranting an outpatient general-physician visit for clinical examination, activity modification guidance, and targeted rehabilitation rather than unguided self-care or emergency care, whereas 10 minutes of slight soreness on the outer side of the right elbow after gripping tools yesterday represents transient post-work muscle fatigue needing only routine home self-care.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts state age 44 and carpentry occupation, daily hand-tool use, and 4 weeks of sharp outer right elbow pain when gripping tools without naming epicondylitis, with a 1-word span difference (19 vs 18 words) and clean 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing. Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice and Rule D, changing only the symptom severity and duration in f3 on the same outer right elbow after gripping tools shifts care cleanly from outpatient physician evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1) with zero stated negatives.
